data.narrative: Alekhya mastered the principles of Context Engineering across Module 03, formulating a layered context architecture (combining system-level conventions with task-specific bundles and negative constraints) for the TaskFlow Team Collaboration feature. During the VERIFY and BREAK phases, she systematically diagnosed convention drift in error formatting, recognizing that the agent defaulted to flat error responses because the context bundle lacked a reusable error utility. She resolved the gap by introducing src/utils/errors.js, updating the context package with concrete usage examples, and refactoring the endpoints to achieve 100% compliance across 14 passing automated tests.

dimension_scores.observation: Engineered layered context packages that balance reusable architectural conventions with task-specific local files and negative guardrails.
dimension_scores.evidence: Constructed progress/context-package.md featuring Part 1 (System-Level Conventions) and Part 2 (Per-Task Bundles for Models, Endpoints, and Memberships).

dimension_scores.observation: Audited generated code against comprehensive convention checklists (naming, error format, imports, file structure) rather than simply checking if tests pass.
dimension_scores.evidence: Identified the error schema inconsistency in src/routes/teams.js ({ error: string } vs { error: { code, message } }) and documented findings in progress/proof_verify_module_03.json.

dimension_scores.observation: Traced the root cause of the convention violation directly to omitted context rather than attempting endless prompt tweaking.
dimension_scores.evidence: Created src/utils/errors.js and updated context packages to provide concrete example grounding, proving that context drives code consistency.

dimension_scores.observation: Selected the Layered Context strategy (Option B) to preserve cross-cutting conventions across tasks while avoiding context window pollution.
dimension_scores.evidence: Articulated clear criteria for the Context Triangle (Architectural, Local, Constraints) and minimum effective context.

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered robust, convention-compliant implementations of teams, routes, and memberships with zero third-party dependencies.
dimension_scores.evidence: 14/14 automated tests passing in tests/*.test.js in under 160ms with zero regressions.
